title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.
   47| 
   48| ## Repository Structure
   49| 
   50| ```
   51| TokenCore/
   52| ├── data/           # Benchmark datasets (also on Hugging Face Hub)
   53| ├── TokenCore.py     # TokenCore method implementation
   54| ├── Demo.ipynb      # End-to-end demo of the key steps
   55| └── README.md
   56| ```
   57|

"""Load the released Grammar benchmark into a canonical document structure.

Source: repo/data/grammar.npy (produced by the authors' tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py
from repo/data/grammar_correction_labeled.json).  The .npy is a 0-d object array
holding a dict with keys 'sentences', 'tokens', 'labels'.
"""
import json
import os

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
REPO = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo")
DATA_DIR = os.path.join(REPO, "data")


def load_grammar():
    """Return list of dicts: {doc_id, sentence, words, token_labels, doc_label}."""
    npy_path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "grammar.npy")
    raw = np.load(npy_path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    sentences = raw["sentences"]
    tokens = raw["tokens"]
    labels = raw["labels"]

    docs = []
    for i, (sent, toks, labs) in enumerate(zip(sentences, tokens, labels)):
        sentence = sent[0] if isinstance(sent, (list, tuple)) else sent
        words = [str(t) for t in toks]
        token_labels = [int(l) for l in labs]
        assert len(words) == len(token_labels), (i, len(words), len(token_labels))
        doc_label = 1 if any(token_labels) else 0
        docs.append(
            {
                "doc_id": i,
                "sentence": sentence,
                "words": words,
                "token_labels": token_labels,
                "doc_label": doc_label,
            }
        )
    return docs


def check_dataset(docs, n_docs=300, n_anom=30):
    """R10: 300 documents, 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% anomaly rate)."""
    assert len(docs) == n_docs, f"expected {n_docs} docs, got {len(docs)}"
    n_anom_docs = sum(d["doc_label"] for d in docs)
    assert n_anom_docs == n_anom, f"expected {n_anom} anomalous docs, got {n_anom_docs}"
    # R11: doc_label == 1 iff at least one token_label == 1
    for d in docs:
        assert d["doc_label"] == (1 if any(d["token_labels"]) else 0)
    return {
        "n_docs": len(docs),
        "n_normal_docs": len(docs) - n_anom_docs,
        "n_anomalous_docs": n_anom_docs,
        "anomaly_rate": n_anom_docs / len(docs),
        "n_tokens_total": sum(len(d["words"]) for d in docs),
        "n_anomalous_tokens_total": sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in docs),
    }


def split_train_test(docs, seed=0, train_frac=0.5):
    """R6: 50% of the *normal* documents are the training set; the remaining
    normal documents plus all anomalous documents form the test set."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    normal_idx = [i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d["doc_label"] == 0]
    anom_idx = [i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d["doc_label"] == 1]
    perm = rng.permutation(len(normal_idx))
    n_train = int(round(train_frac * len(normal_idx)))
    train_idx = [normal_idx[p] for p in perm[:n_train]]
    test_idx = [normal_idx[p] for p in perm[n_train:]] + list(anom_idx)
    train_docs = [docs[i] for i in train_idx]
    test_docs = [docs[i] for i in test_idx]
    return train_docs, test_docs


if __name__ == "__main__":
    docs = load_grammar()
    print(json.dumps(check_dataset(docs), indent=2))
    tr, te = split_train_test(docs, seed=0)
    print("train docs:", len(tr), "test docs:", len(te))
    print("train anomalous tokens:", sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in tr))
    print("test anomalous tokens:", sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in te))
    print("test tokens:", sum(len(d["words"]) for d in te))
    print("example anomalous doc:", [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1][0])

"""BERT-base front-end: word-level embeddings by element-wise max pooling over subwords.

This is the batched equivalent of the authors' ``align.extract_word_embeddings``
(kept verbatim in repo/align.py): last hidden state, [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] dropped,
subwords grouped by ``word_ids()`` and element-wise max-pooled per word (Eq. 1).
"""
import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer


def load_backbone(model_name, device="cpu"):
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, use_fast=True)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model.to(device).eval()
    return tok, model


@torch.no_grad()
def extract_word_embeddings(docs, tokenizer, model, device="cpu", batch_size=32,
                            max_length=128, verbose=False):
    """Return (X, y, doc_ids) where X[i] is the max-pooled word embedding of the
    i-th word unit, y[i] its gold token label and doc_ids[i] its document index."""
    all_words = [d["words"] for d in docs]
    all_labels = [d["token_labels"] for d in docs]

    X_parts, y_parts, doc_parts = [], [], []
    n_dropped = 0
    for start in range(0, len(docs), batch_size):
        chunk_docs = list(range(start, min(start + batch_size, len(docs))))
        enc = tokenizer(
            [all_words[i] for i in chunk_docs],
            is_split_into_words=True,
            return_tensors="pt",
            padding=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
        )
        enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
        out = model(input_ids=enc["input_ids"], attention_mask=enc["attention_mask"])
        hs = out.last_hidden_state  # (B, L, H)

        for b, di in enumerate(chunk_docs):
            wids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=b)
            groups = {}
            for pos, wid in enumerate(wids):
                if wid is None:
                    continue  # [CLS] / [SEP] / [PAD]
                groups.setdefault(wid, []).append(pos)
            words = all_words[di]
            labels = all_labels[di]
            if len(groups) != len(words):
                n_dropped += len(words) - len(groups)
                if verbose:
                    print(f"  doc {di}: {len(words)} words -> {len(groups)} units "
                          f"(truncated at max_length={max_length})")
            order = sorted(groups)
            idx = torch.tensor([groups[w] for w in order], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            sub = hs[b][idx]                      # (n_words, n_sub, H)
            pooled = sub.max(dim=1).values        # element-wise max over subwords
            X_parts.append(pooled.cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32))
            y_parts.append(np.asarray([labels[w] for w in order], dtype=np.int64))
            doc_parts.append(np.full(len(order), di, dtype=np.int64))

    X = np.concatenate(X_parts, axis=0)
    y = np.concatenate(y_parts, axis=0)
    doc_ids = np.concatenate(doc_parts, axis=0)
    return X, y, doc_ids, n_dropped


def check_max_pooling(docs, tokenizer, model, device="cpu"):
    """Hand-check that pooling really is the coordinate-wise max of subword vectors."""
    d = docs[0]
    enc = tokenizer([d["words"]], is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                    padding=False, truncation=True, max_length=128)
    enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
    with torch.no_grad():
        hs = model(**enc).last_hidden_state[0].cpu().numpy()
    wids = enc.word_ids(batch_index=0)
    groups = {}
    for pos, wid in enumerate(wids):
        if wid is not None:
            groups.setdefault(wid, []).append(pos)
    for wid in sorted(groups)[:3]:
        manual = np.max(np.stack([hs[p] for p in groups[wid]]), axis=0)
        assert manual.shape == (hs.shape[1],)
    return hs.shape[1]

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified repo/TokenCore.py."""
import importlib.util
import os

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
TOKENCORE_PY = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "TokenCore.py")


def _load_module():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("authors_tokencore", TOKENCORE_PY)
    mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(mod)
    return mod


def make_detector():
    """Instantiate the authors' TokenCore exactly as in the README quick start."""
    mod = _load_module()
    if not hasattr(mod, "TokenCore"):
        raise RuntimeError("authors' TokenCore.py does not define class TokenCore")
    return mod.TokenCore()


def fit_score(X_train, X_test):
    """Fit the memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3) and
    return one nearest-neighbour distance per test token (R4)."""
    det = make_detector()
    det.fit(X_train)
    return det.decision_function(X_test)

"""Metric layer: pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC and mean-aggregated document-level scores."""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score


def token_level_metrics(scores, labels):
    """Micro: pool all test tokens of all test documents into one ranking (A5)."""
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    labels = np.asarray(labels, dtype=np.int64)
    assert scores.shape == labels.shape
    if len(np.unique(labels)) < 2:
        return {"auroc": float("nan"), "auprc": float("nan")}
    return {
        "auroc": float(roc_auc_score(labels, scores)),
        "auprc": float(average_precision_score(labels, scores)),
    }


def document_scores(scores, doc_ids):
    """Eq. (3): arithmetic mean of the token scores within each document."""
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    doc_ids = np.asarray(doc_ids)
    uniq = np.unique(doc_ids)
    out = np.empty(len(uniq), dtype=np.float64)
    for i, d in enumerate(uniq):
        out[i] = scores[doc_ids == d].mean()
    return uniq, out


def document_level_metrics(scores, doc_ids, doc_labels):
    uniq, doc_scores = document_scores(scores, doc_ids)
    lab = np.asarray([doc_labels[d] for d in uniq], dtype=np.int64)
    return token_level_metrics(doc_scores, lab), doc_scores, lab


def metric_parity_check():
    """Verify our AUROC/AUPRC plumbing against sklearn on synthetic labels."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    y = rng.randint(0, 2, 500)
    s = rng.rand(500)
    a = roc_auc_score(y, s)
    p = average_precision_score(y, s)
    assert 0.0 <= a <= 1.0 and 0.0 <= p <= 1.0
    # perfect separation must give 1.0
    assert roc_auc_score(y, y.astype(float)) == 1.0
    return {"synthetic_auroc": float(a), "synthetic_auprc": float(p)}

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (paper Table 1).

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5 + Sec. 6.1):
  data_grammar  -> released 300-doc Grammar benchmark (270 normal / 30 anomalous)
  split         -> 50% of the normal documents train the memory bank, the rest
                   (normal + anomalous) is the test set
  embed_bert    -> BERT-base-uncased, last hidden state, element-wise max pooling
                   over subwords to word level (Eq. 1)
  detector      -> authors' TokenCore memory bank + nearest-neighbour scoring (Eq. 2)
  evaluate      -> pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC, mean-aggregated document level (Eq. 3)

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                     # full Grammar run, seed 0
  python reproduce.py --smoke             # 10-document smoke test
  python reproduce.py --seeds 0 1 2       # multi-seed spread
  python reproduce.py --model bert-base-cased   # sensitivity (notebook used cased)

import json

import sys
import time

os.environ.setdefault("TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM", "false")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY", "1")

import torch  # noqa: E402

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402
from detector import fit_score  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import extract_word_embeddings, load_backbone  # noqa: E402

TARGET_AUROC = 0.6371  # paper Table 1, Token section, TokenCore, Grammar ROC
TOLERANCE = 0.02


def run_once(model_name, seed, smoke=False, batch_size=32, max_length=128,
             device="cpu", verbose=True):
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    stats = data_grammar.check_dataset(docs)

    if smoke:
        normal = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 0][:8]
        anom = [d for d in docs if d["doc_label"] == 1][:2]
        train_docs, test_docs = normal[:6], normal[6:] + anom
    else:
        train_docs, test_docs = data_grammar.split_train_test(docs, seed=seed)

    tok, model = load_backbone(model_name, device=device)

    X_train, y_train, _, _ = extract_word_embeddings(
        train_docs, tok, model, device=device, batch_size=batch_size,
        max_length=max_length, verbose=verbose)
    X_test, y_test, doc_ids_test, n_dropped = extract_word_embeddings(
        test_docs, tok, model, device=device, batch_size=batch_size,
        max_length=max_length, verbose=verbose)

    assert X_train.shape[1] == 768, X_train.shape
    assert int(y_train.sum()) == 0, "training set must contain no anomalous tokens (R3)"

    scores = fit_score(X_train, X_test)

    tok_m = evaluate.token_level_metrics(scores, y_test)
    doc_labels = {d["doc_id"]: d["doc_label"] for d in test_docs}
    doc_m, doc_scores, doc_lab = evaluate.document_level_metrics(
        scores, doc_ids_test, doc_labels)

    # control: random scores
    rng = np.random.RandomState(123)
    rand_m = evaluate.token_level_metrics(rng.rand(len(y_test)), y_test)

    out = {
        "model": model_name,
        "seed": seed,
        "smoke": smoke,
        "n_docs": stats["n_docs"],
        "n_train_docs": len(train_docs),
        "n_test_docs": len(test_docs),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(X_train.shape[0]),
        "n_test_tokens": int(X_test.shape[0]),
        "n_positive_tokens": int(y_test.sum()),
        "token_positive_rate": float(y_test.mean()),
        "n_dropped_word_units": int(n_dropped),
        "token_auroc": tok_m["auroc"],
        "token_auprc": tok_m["auprc"],
        "doc_auroc": doc_m["auroc"],
        "doc_auprc": doc_m["auprc"],
        "random_token_auroc": rand_m["auroc"],
        "random_token_auprc": rand_m["auprc"],
    }
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="bert-base-uncased")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="*", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=128)

"""Verify that batched (padded) inference equals the authors' one-sentence-at-a-time
inference, and that max pooling is the coordinate-wise max of subword vectors."""
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", os.path.join(
    os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(HERE, ".cache")), "hf"))
os.environ.setdefault("TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM", "false")

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import torch  # noqa: E402

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import extract_word_embeddings, load_backbone  # noqa: E402

docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
tok, model = load_backbone("bert-base-cased")

# 1) batched vs single-sentence (padding=False), the authors' align.py path
sub = docs[:12]
Xb, yb, db, _ = extract_word_embeddings(sub, tok, model, batch_size=32, max_length=128)
Xs, ys, ds, _ = extract_word_embeddings(sub, tok, model, batch_size=1, max_length=128)
print("batched shape:", Xb.shape, "single shape:", Xs.shape)
print("max abs diff batched-vs-single:", float(np.abs(Xb - Xs).max()))
assert np.allclose(Xb, Xs, atol=1e-4), "batching changed the embeddings"
assert np.array_equal(yb, ys) and np.array_equal(db, ds)

# 2) max pooling is the coordinate-wise max of the word's subword vectors
d = docs[0]
enc = tok([d["words"]], is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt", padding=False,
          truncation=True, max_length=128)
enc_a = tok([d["words"]], is_split_into_words=True, padding=False, truncation=True,
            max_length=128)
with torch.no_grad():
    hs = model(**enc).last_hidden_state[0].cpu().numpy()
wids = enc_a.word_ids(batch_index=0)
groups = {}
for pos, wid in enumerate(wids):
    if wid is not None:
        groups.setdefault(wid, []).append(pos)
X1, _, _, _ = extract_word_embeddings([d], tok, model, batch_size=1, max_length=128)
for wid in sorted(groups):
    manual = np.max(np.stack([hs[p] for p in groups[wid]]), axis=0)
    assert np.allclose(manual, X1[wid], atol=1e-5), wid
print("max-pooling verified on", len(groups), "word units of doc 0; hidden width",
      hs.shape[1])
assert hs.shape[1] == 768

# 3) alignment coverage: every gold word gets exactly one unit
Xall, yall, dall, dropped = extract_word_embeddings(docs, tok, model, batch_size=32,
                                                    max_length=128)
n_gold = sum(len(d["words"]) for d in docs)
print("gold words:", n_gold, "word units:", Xall.shape[0], "dropped:", dropped)
assert Xall.shape[0] == n_gold, "alignment is not 1:1"
assert np.array_equal(yall, np.concatenate([d["token_labels"] for d in docs]))
print("ALL CHECKS PASSED")

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (paper Table 1).

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5 + Sec. 6.1):
  data_grammar  -> released 300-doc Grammar benchmark (270 normal / 30 anomalous)
  split         -> 50% of the normal documents train the memory bank, the rest
                   (normal + anomalous) is the test set
  embed_bert    -> BERT-base, last hidden state, element-wise max pooling over
                   subwords to word level (Eq. 1)
  detector      -> authors' TokenCore memory bank + nearest-neighbour scoring (Eq. 2)
  evaluate      -> pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC, mean-aggregated document level (Eq. 3)

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                          # full Grammar run, 10 seeds
  python reproduce.py --smoke                  # 10-document smoke test
  python reproduce.py --seeds 0 1 2            # chosen seeds
  python reproduce.py --model bert-base-uncased
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SRC = os.path.join(HERE, "src")
sys.path.insert(0, SRC)

# Cache the backbone in the shared REPRO_DATA_CACHE so a clean re-run needs no download.
_CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(HERE, ".cache"))
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", os.path.join(_CACHE, "hf"))
os.environ.setdefault("TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM", "false")

def run_once(model_name, seed, backbone, smoke=False, batch_size=32, max_length=128,
             verbose=True):
    """One full TokenCore run on Grammar. Returns a dict of metrics."""
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    data_grammar.check_dataset(docs)
    train_docs, test_docs = data_grammar.split_train_test(docs, seed=seed, smoke=smoke)
    doc_labels = {d["doc_id"]: d["doc_label"] for d in test_docs}

    tok, model = backbone
    X_train, y_train, _, _ = extract_word_embeddings(
        train_docs, tok, model, batch_size=batch_size, max_length=max_length)
    X_test, y_test, doc_ids_test, dropped = extract_word_embeddings(
        test_docs, tok, model, batch_size=batch_size, max_length=max_length)

    assert y_train.sum() == 0, "memory bank must contain no anomalous tokens (R3)"
    assert X_train.shape[1] == 768, X_train.shape

    scores = fit_score(X_train, X_test)

    tok_m = evaluate.token_level_metrics(scores, y_test)
    doc_m, doc_scores, doc_lab = evaluate.document_level_metrics(
        scores, doc_ids_test, doc_labels)
    rng = evaluate.np.random.RandomState(seed)
    ctrl = evaluate.token_level_metrics(rng.rand(len(scores)), y_test)

    r = {
        "seed": seed,
        "token_auroc": tok_m["auroc"],
        "token_auprc": tok_m["auprc"],
        "doc_auroc": doc_m["auroc"],
        "doc_auprc": doc_m["auprc"],
        "n_train_docs": len(train_docs),
        "n_test_docs": len(test_docs),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(X_train.shape[0]),
        "n_test_tokens": int(X_test.shape[0]),
        "n_positive_tokens": int(y_test.sum()),
        "token_positive_rate": float(y_test.mean()),
        "random_control_token_auroc": ctrl["auroc"],
        "n_dropped_words": dropped,
    }
    if verbose:
        print("[seed %d] token AUROC=%.4f AUPRC=%.4f | doc AUROC=%.4f AUPRC=%.4f | "
              "bank=%d test_tokens=%d pos=%d"
              % (seed, r["token_auroc"], r["token_auprc"], r["doc_auroc"],
                 r["doc_auprc"], r["n_bank_tokens"], r["n_test_tokens"],
                 r["n_positive_tokens"]), flush=True)

def summarise(per_seed):
    aurocs = [r["token_auroc"] for r in per_seed]

        "multi_seed_mean_token_auprc": float(evaluate.np.mean(auprcs)),

args.content:
"""Ablations over the choices the paper does not pin down, at fixed seed 0.

Run under bert-base-uncased (the backbone the paper text / contract R1 names).
Each variant changes exactly one thing from the faithful configuration, which is
itself fixed by the authors' own repo/align.py:
  * last hidden state only (align.py line 84)          -> A3
  * one unit per gold word token, punctuation included -> A4
  * raw embeddings + sklearn NearestNeighbors default  -> A9/A1
"""
import json
import os
import sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", os.path.join(
    os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(HERE, ".cache")), "hf"))
os.environ.setdefault("TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM", "false")

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import torch  # noqa: E402

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402
from detector import fit_score  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import extract_word_embeddings, load_backbone  # noqa: E402

MODEL = "bert-base-uncased"
SEED = 0
PUNCT = set(".,;:!?\"'()[]{}<>-–—/\\|@#$%^&*+=~`")


def is_punct(w):
    return all(c in PUNCT for c in w)


def run(backbone, layers=None, l2norm=False, drop_punct=False):
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    train_docs, test_docs = data_grammar.split_train_test(docs, seed=SEED)
    doc_labels = {d["doc_id"]: d["doc_label"] for d in test_docs}
    tok, model = backbone

    def emb(ds):
        X, y, dids, _ = extract_word_embeddings(ds, tok, model, layers=layers)
        if drop_punct:
            keep = np.array([not is_punct(w) for d in ds for w in d["words"]])
            X, y, dids = X[keep], y[keep], dids[keep]
        if l2norm:
            X = X / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-12)
        return X, y, dids

    Xtr, ytr, _ = emb(train_docs)
    Xte, yte, dids = emb(test_docs)
    scores = fit_score(Xtr, Xte)
    m = evaluate.token_level_metrics(scores, yte)
    dm, _, _ = evaluate.document_level_metrics(scores, dids, doc_labels)
    return {"token_auroc": m["auroc"], "token_auprc": m["auprc"],
            "doc_auroc": dm["auroc"], "n_test_tokens": int(len(yte)),
            "n_positive_tokens": int(yte.sum())}


def main():
    torch.set_num_threads(7)
    backbone = load_backbone(MODEL)
    variants = {
        "faithful_last_layer_raw_euclid_all_units": {},
        "A3_mean_of_last_4_layers": {"layers": 4},
        "A9A1_l2_normalized_embeddings": {"l2norm": True},
        "A4_drop_punctuation_units": {"drop_punct": True},
    }
    out = {"backbone": MODEL, "seed": SEED, "target_value": 0.6371, "variants": {}}
    for name, kw in variants.items():
        r = run(backbone, **kw)
        out["variants"][name] = r
        print("%-42s token AUROC=%.4f AUPRC=%.4f doc AUROC=%.4f (n_test=%d pos=%d)"
              % (name, r["token_auroc"], r["token_auprc"], r["doc_auroc"],
                 r["n_test_tokens"], r["n_positive_tokens"]), flush=True)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(HERE, "results"), exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(HERE, "results", "ablations.json"), "w",
              encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print("wrote results/ablations.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

args.summary:
## Target claim C1: TokenCore token-level AUROC on Grammar — reproduced with a documented backbone conflict

`python reproduce.py` runs end-to-end from a clean `results/` in **~5 min** (limit 20 min), CPU-only, and writes `results/metrics.json`.

### What was rebuilt
The authors shipped the method (`repo/TokenCore.py`), the pooling/alignment helper (`repo/align.py`) and all three annotated datasets, but **no runnable entrypoint** — only a 3.8 MB `Demo.ipynb` with frozen outputs, and `TokenCore.py` consumes precomputed embedding matrices. I kept the authors' files verbatim and rebuilt the missing driver: `src/data_grammar.py` (loads `grammar.npy`, asserts 300 docs / 270 normal / 30 anomalous = 10% rate, R10), `src/embed_bert.py` (batched BERT, last hidden state, element-wise max-pool over subwords per Eq. 1), `src/detector.py` (thin adapter over the unmodified `TokenCore.py`), `src/evaluate.py` (pooled token AUROC/AUPRC + mean-aggregated document level, Eq. 3).

### Results (10 random 50/50 splits, seeds 0–9)

| | backbone | token AUROC | token AUPRC | vs 0.6371 ±0.02 | pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PRIMARY** (R1-faithful) | bert-base-**uncased** | 0.5793 ± 0.0302 | 0.0335 ± 0.0026 | err 0.0578 | **False** |
| **SECONDARY** (released code default) | bert-base-**cased** | 0.6268 ± 0.0212 | 0.0376 ± 0.0021 | err 0.0103 | **True** |

### The backbone conflict (the substantive finding)
The paper text (Sec. 6.1, R1) says **bert-base-uncased**; the authors' released code says **bert-base-cased** (`align.py` default `model_name`, and `Demo.ipynb` cell 0). I initially made cased the default because it landed closer to the target — that is circular reasoning (fitting to the target), so I reversed it: **uncased is now primary on R1 grounds**, and cased is a labelled secondary justified *only* by being the released code default. Both numbers and both pass/fail flags are in `metrics.json` under `backbone_conflict`, with no proximity-based justification anywhere.

### Verification performed
